slides.heading: Employment Landscape
lines: KP population above 40 M | Young & growing fast
Large youth cohort enters the labour market every year
Agriculture & services remain the main employers
Most jobs are informal | Low pay | No protection
Female labour force participation remains very low
Remittances from the Gulf sustain many households
Merged districts lag far behind on jobs & services
sources: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population & Housing Census, 2023
Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, Labour Force Survey 2020-21
UNDP, Pakistan National Human Development Report: Youth, 2017

slides.heading: Key Challenges
lines: Job creation lags behind labour force growth
Weak industrial base | Few large employers
Energy costs & shortfalls hold back manufacturing
Security concerns deter private investment
Limited access to finance for small firms
Poor connectivity in southern & merged districts
Skills taught do not match what employers need
sources: World Bank, Pakistan Development Update, 2024
Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, Labour Force Survey 2020-21
State Bank of Pakistan, Annual Report on the State of the Economy, 2024

slides.heading: Skills Mismatch
lines: Graduates seek government jobs | Few exist
General degrees outnumber technical qualifications
Training courses outdated | Equipment obsolete
Employers rarely shape curricula or standards
Little career guidance in schools & colleges
Weak tracking of graduates after training
Overseas employers demand certified skills
sources: NAVTTC, National Skills Strategy 2009-2013
ADB, Pakistan Country Diagnostic: Skills Development, 2019
Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment, Annual Report, 2023

slides.heading: TVET Reform
lines: Make KP TEVTA demand-driven & performance-based
Adopt competency-based training & assessment
Industry boards to set courses for every trade
Upgrade labs & retrain instructors in new trades
Add digital, solar, construction & hospitality skills
Align certificates with the National Vocational Framework
Fund institutes on graduate job placement
sources: Government of KP, KP TEVTA Act, 2015
NAVTTC, National Vocational Qualifications Framework, 2017
ADB, Pakistan Country Diagnostic: Skills Development, 2019

slides.heading: Growth Centres
lines: Rashakai SEZ as the anchor for CPEC industry
Activate existing economic zones before building new
District clusters around local strengths
Marble | Minerals | Fruit Processing | Tourism
Plug-and-play sheds for small manufacturers
Link each centre to a nearby training institute
Roads | Power | Gas before tenants arrive
sources: KP Economic Zones Development & Management Company, Economic Zones Portfolio, 2023
Board of Investment, Special Economic Zones Act, 2012
CPEC Authority, Long Term Plan for CPEC 2017-2030

slides.heading: Private Sector Links
lines: Industry to co-design courses & assessments
Paid apprenticeships in partner firms
Wage subsidies for first-time hires
Chambers to share annual demand for skills
Public-private management of selected institutes
Ease of doing business through one-window services
Link trainees to overseas employment agencies
sources: Government of Pakistan, Apprenticeship Act, 2018
KP Board of Investment & Trade, Investment Facilitation Framework, 2023
World Bank, Doing Business in Pakistan, 2020

slides.heading: Youth & Women
lines: Self-employment loans for young entrepreneurs
Startup incubators in every divisional headquarters
Freelancing & IT training for online income
Home-based & digital work for women
Safe transport & childcare near training centres
Special quotas for merged district youth
Mentoring | Market Access | Follow-up Support
sources: Government of KP, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Youth Policy, 2016
UNDP, Pakistan National Human Development Report: Youth, 2017
ILO, Women's Economic Empowerment in Pakistan, 2020

slides.heading: Financing & Delivery
lines: Pool skills funding into one KP jobs fund
Results-based contracts with training providers
Use World Bank & ADB support for economic zones
Credit guarantees for small & medium firms
A labour market information system for KP
Annual report on jobs created by district
Low Cost | High Impact | Measured Results
sources: World Bank, KP Economic Revitalization Project, Project Appraisal Document, 2020
State Bank of Pakistan, Prime Minister Youth Business & Agriculture Loan Scheme, 2023

slides.heading: Way Forward
lines: Set a provincial jobs target with clear owners
Reform TEVTA within 12 months
Fully activate Rashakai & two district clusters
Sign apprenticeship deals with leading chambers
Launch youth & women employment window
Track jobs quarterly | Publish results openly
CMPO to coordinate | Departments to deliver
sources: Government of KP, KP TEVTA Act, 2015
CPEC Authority, Long Term Plan for CPEC 2017-2030
Government of KP, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Youth Policy, 2016
